default), `flex` or `grid`.

overflow.description:

`nowrap` (the default), `wrap` or `wrap_reverse`.

max_width.description:
The picture fits in this many pixels across and down, keeping its
shape (never larger than the target itself); full size if absent.

slots.description:

target.description:

required.description:

live H.264), rather than a diagnostic cell.

direction.description:

`recording.iso.encoder.bit_depth` (an 8 here stays 8 even at the
incredible preset). 10-bit HEVC uses the Main 10 profile, which
avoids banding in gradients, at more encoder work and bigger files;
a display, window or application is then also captured in 10 bits.

the file follows the recording settings.

SourceMask.description:
Uses another source's or scene's live picture as the mask (OBS
Advanced Masks' source masks), frame by frame in step with the
program. Until the mask has a picture, nothing of the source shows,
whatever `invert`, `threshold` or `combine` say. Previews of the source
alone, and its ISO file, show it unmasked by other sources.

invert.description:
Show the picture where the mask would hide it, and hide it where
it would show.

mask_scene.description: Or the id of a scene, drawn on its own canvas, that masks.

mask_source.description:
The id of the video source whose picture masks (give it or
`mask_scene`). It runs, and is on air (media play, pages load),
while a source it masks does.

scale.description: Scales the mask's picture about its centre, after `fit`.

softness.description:
How gradually it turns, 0 (at once: a hard edge) to 1 (evenly from
0 to 1, which with a threshold of 0.5 uses the value as it is).

threshold.description:
With `softness`, where the channel's value turns from hiding to
showing the picture: 0 to 1.

x.description:
Where the mask's centre is across the masked picture: 0 (left) to
1 (right).

What `speed_test` measured, or why it couldn't, and the stream bitrate
it recommends either way.

method.description:
How: `acknowledged` (bytes the server said it received over time) or
`sent` (bytes the connection took once its buffers were full).

reason.description: Why it wasn't measured, if it wasn't.

recommended_kbps.description: The stream bitrate for it, kb/s.

live setup's, if absent. Required for custom and Kick.

absent.

folder.description:
Record into a new project folder in this folder instead of the
setup's `recording.folder` (or into this folder, if it is a
project's: the new take joins that project).

seconds.description: Stop on its own after this many seconds.

setup.description: The setup to record; the live setup if absent.

already_recording.description:
`start` was asked again with the same params while this session
was already recording (or starting): nothing new started, and this
is the running session.

begins_at.description:
When a split's new take begins (local time, RFC 3339 with
milliseconds): the next whole second, a moment after the split.
Frames and audio before then are in the take before.

notes.description:
Things to know, like a setup given to `start` replacing the live
setup.

session.description:
The recording session's id: give it to `stop` and `request_stop`
so they can only end this session. Absent for a split's new take
(the session is the same).

canvases.description:
Every canvas besides the main one (`[vertical]` first, then
`[[canvases]]`, #84): its size, scene, preview, streams, replay
buffer and recording. The `vertical_*` fields above stay for clients
of the vertical canvas alone.

collection.description: The scene collection and profile in use, once there is a live setup.

cpu_percent.description:
How much of this Mac's processor isocastd used lately, in percent
of all its cores (as OBS's status bar shows it): measured between
readings at least a second apart.

daemon.description:
Which isocastd answered: its version and build, so a client can
tell an engine left running from before an app update.

data.description: The data store: its keys, size, writes and events.

diagnostics.description: Log health and previous launches lacking a clean-exit marker.

engine.description: The live engine, while it runs.

files.description: Files the running session is writing.

finalizing.description:
A stop has been requested for the running session (or its start
cancelled) and it hasn't ended yet. This says the request was
accepted, not where the files were cut or that they are on disk.
Until it ends, `start`, `pause`, `resume` and `split` are refused;
then `last` (or `last_error`) and the `stopped` event give the
outcome.

last.description: The report of the most recent finished session.

last_error.description:
Why the most recent session ended without a report: it failed to
start (after `start` returned, too) or was stopped while starting.
`last` is then an earlier session's. Cleared when a session ends
with a report.

live.description: The running session's live counters, once it has started.

load_warning.description:
A current episode of reduced system/encoder headroom; clears after
recovery, not on a new take. Events are limited to one `warning` per
cause every three minutes; status still shows suppressed episodes.
Latency and CPU detection are blind for five seconds after our encoder
sessions change (including a split), while a new baseline is learned.
Thermal and encoder-allocation failure warnings do not need that baseline.

machine_profile.description: A compact calibration summary; machine_profile returns the measurements.

preview.description: The scene staged in preview, if any.

program_bytes_per_second.description:
How fast the live setup's program file fills that disk, at most:
the generous estimate the free-space check plans for, in bytes per
second (`ProgramRecording::bytes_per_second`). Absent without a
setup, or when the program isn't recorded.

recording_free_bytes.description:
Free space on the disk the live setup records to (its
`recording.folder`, or the nearest folder above it that exists;
with no setup yet, `~/Movies/Isocast`'s, where a new one records),
in bytes, as the daemon may use it: measured with each status.

replay.description: The replay buffer: running or not, what it holds, its last save.

scene.description: The scene on air (an id), if the setup has scenes.

session.description:
The running session's id (while starting, recording or
finalizing), as `stop` and `request_stop` take it.

setup_file.description: Where the live setup is kept between runs, and whether it loaded.

stream.description:
The stream, if the live setup streams or a stream is running: the
main destination's (see `streams` for every destination).

streams.description:
Every stream destination, the main one first (empty without a
`[stream]` section or a running stream).

vertical_preview.description:
The scene staged in the vertical canvas's own preview, if any
(while it follows the main canvas, the main preview's).

vertical_replay.description:
The vertical canvas's replay buffer (`canvas: vertical`), while the
setup has a vertical canvas or its buffer ran; kept apart from
`replay` so clients of the main canvas see only its buffer.

vertical_scene.description:
The scene on air on the vertical canvas (an id), if the live setup
has one: the main scene while it follows the main canvas.

vertical_streams.description:
Every vertical stream destination (`[vertical.stream]`), the main
one first, each with `canvas: vertical`; kept apart from `streams`
so clients of the main canvas see only its streams.

virtual_camera.description: Camera output state (installation is explicit, never automatic).

oneOf.description: At the start of each step: the first jump is at once.
At the end of each step: the last jump is at the end.
At both ends: n + 1 levels, from 0 to 1, each held as long.

At neither: n levels from 0 to 1, the first and last held as long as
the others.

position.description:
Where each step jumps: `start`, `end` (the default), `both` or
`none`.

Stinger.description:
A video played over the switch (OBS's Stinger). It lasts as long as the
video. Transparent parts need a video with alpha (ProRes 4444 or HEVC
with alpha in a .mov, or VP9 or VP8 with alpha in a .webm, as OBS uses),
or a matte.

cut_point_ms.description:
When the scenes switch behind the video, in milliseconds from its
start; half way through if absent. Not used with a matte.

file.description:
The video: absolute, `~/...`, or relative to the setup file. It
must be in the setup's transitions when a recording starts, which
loads it.

matte.description:
A track matte in the same video (OBS's track matte): where it is
white the next scene shows, where black the current one, and grey
blends them; the video's other half plays on top.

no_password.description:
